name: drying rack
hint: A rack on which fish or meat dries for 12 hours. Process one batch at a time; use meat's dry action to hang it.

log: You drive two logs into the sand by the fire and lay a third across them.
Two uprights, a crossbar: a rack beside the fire, where the smoke drifts.
You erect the rack downwind of the hearth, where fish and meat may dry slowly.

start.label: hang fish
log: You clean and split two fish before hanging them from the crossbar.
Two prepared fish are suspended on the rack to dry.
You arrange the fish where the rising smoke can reach them.

collect.label: take down
log: The preserved food has become firm and dark during its time above the fire.
Dry, hard, smelling of smoke. They will keep.
The food leaves the rack thoroughly dry, and should now keep far longer.

readyLog: The food upon the rack has become sufficiently dry for storage.
The provisions have finished drying and may now be collected.
